title: RPM: Add versions to our "Obsoletes" declarations.
description:
Blind attempt at fixing

RPM build errors:
    line 230: It's not recommended to have unversioned Obsoletes: Obsoletes:	wireshark-gnome wireshark-gtk

on Fedora 33.

notes.body:
Our builds started breaking because Fedora 33 was released, which was automatically picked up due to an unversioned/untagged "image: fedora" in .gitlab-ci.yml. Should we use "image: fedora:32" instead?

Also, we have our own [Ubuntu](https://github.com/wireshark/wireshark-ubuntu-dev-docker) and [Windows](https://github.com/wireshark/wireshark-windows-dev-docker) docker images, which have a bunch of prerequisites installed. We don't have images for Fedora, CentOS, or openSUSE. Should we?

added 1 commit
  • e51ee51b - RPM: Add versions to our "Obsoletes" declarations.
[Compare with previous version](/wireshark/wireshark/-/merge_requests/747/diffs?diff_id=120773271&start_sha=1c85775c3fe5aa8fa429a4791d862d9980cfc72c)
This didn't fix it: https://gitlab.com/geraldcombs/wireshark/-/pipelines/208338972

You're still getting the "ninja: error: loading 'build.ninja': No such file or directory" error.  Perhaps the Shiny New CMake in Fedora 33 doesn't bother building one of those boring old "build.ninja" files if invoked with "-G Ninja", or perhaps the Shiny New Ninja in Fedora 33 doesn't bother reading those boring old files any more, or some other "compatibility is for wimps" improvement?

The Fedora output shows that it's passing `-B` to cmake:

> \+ /usr/bin/cmake -S . -B x86_64-redhat-linux-gnu -DCMAKE_C_FLAGS_RELEASE:STRING=-DNDEBUG -DCMAKE_CXX_FLAGS_RELEASE:STRING=-DNDEBUG -DCMAKE_Fortran_FLAGS_RELEASE:STRING=-DNDEBUG -DCMAKE_VERBOSE_MAKEFILE:BOOL=ON -DCMAKE_INSTALL_PREFIX:PATH=/usr/local -DINCLUDE_INSTALL_DIR:PATH=/usr/local/include -DLIB_INSTALL_DIR:PATH=/usr/local/lib64 -DSYSCONF_INSTALL_DIR:PATH=/etc -DSHARE_INSTALL_PREFIX:PATH=/usr/local/share -DLIB_SUFFIX=64 -DBUILD_SHARED_LIBS:BOOL=ON -DCMAKE_INSTALL_PREFIX=/usr/local -DBUILD_wireshark=ON -DENABLE_LUA=ON -DBUILD_mmdbresolve=ON -DENABLE_LZ4=ON -DENABLE_SNAPPY=ON -DENABLE_SPANDSP=ON -DENABLE_BCG729=OFF -DENABLE_LIBXML2=ON -DENABLE_NGHTTP2=ON -DBUILD_sdjournal=ON -DENABLE_BROTLI=ON -DDISABLE_WERROR=ON -G Ninja -DENABLE_ILBC=ON -DENABLE_OPUS=ON

while the CentOS and openSUSE don't. We call the "%cmake" macro in our .spec file instead of calling cmake directly, which would appear to explain the discrepancy. The [Fedora CMake packaging guidelines](https://docs.fedoraproject.org/en-US/packaging-guidelines/CMake/) mention %cmake_build and %cmake_install macros. I'm guessing that they handle the `-B` flag.

changes_data.diff:
@@ -226,6 +226,7 @@ Wireshark. A Qt graphical user interface is packaged separately.
 %package	qt
 Summary:	Wireshark's Qt-based GUI
 Group:		Applications/Internet
+# XXX Fedora 33 requires versioned "Obsoletes" declarations.
 Obsoletes:	wireshark-gnome wireshark-gtk
 %description qt
 This package contains the Qt Wireshark GUI and desktop integration files.
@@ -281,6 +282,11 @@ development of Wireshark scripts and plugins.
 %define _bindir /usr/bin
 %endif
 
+# XXX How do we reliably run CMake for all of CentOS, Fedora, RHEL, and openSUSE?
+# The percent-cmake macro in Fedora >= 33 runs
+# /usr/bin/cmake -S . -B x86_64-redhat-linux-gnu
+# which presumably means we need to use the cmake_build and cmake_install
+# macros described at https://docs.fedoraproject.org/en-US/packaging-guidelines/CMake/
 %if 0%{?rhel}
 cmake3 \
 %else

@@ -99,7 +99,9 @@ test:rpm-opensuse-15.1:
     GIT_STRATEGY: none
   dependencies:
     - build:rpm-opensuse-15.1
-build:rpm-fedora:
+
+# Disabled for now due to issues with Fedora 33.
+.build:rpm-fedora:
   <<: *build-rpm
   image: fedora
   script:
@@ -109,7 +111,8 @@ build:rpm-fedora:
     - cd build
     - cmake3 -GNinja ..
     - ninja-build rpm-package
-test:rpm-fedora:
+
+.test:rpm-fedora:
   image: fedora
   stage: test
   script:
@@ -263,7 +266,7 @@ merge-req:ubuntu-clang-other-tests:
   artifacts:
     paths:
       - cppcheck_report.xml
-      - cppcheck_report.html  
+      - cppcheck_report.html

Fedora 33's RPM environent added changes that break CMake. Disable it
for now.
